subject: Agriculture
title: The CGIAR System
description: A fast breakdown of The CGIAR System for builders.

hook.text: CIMMYT and IRRI were just the start. Today, 15 research centers across the world breed crops for the poor.

buildup.text: CGIAR—the Consultative Group on International Agricultural Research—coordinates global crop science.

discovery.text: These centers have released thousands of improved varieties—drought-tolerant maize, flood-proof rice, biofortified beans.

twist.text: Funding is shrinking. Donor fatigue and competing priorities threaten the system that feeds millions.

climax.text: CGIAR's work is public. Unlike corporate seeds, their varieties are free for any farmer to grow.

punchline.text: The world's crop insurance system runs on public science—underfunded.

quiz.question: What makes CGIAR crop varieties different from corporate seeds?
options: They're released as public goods, free for any farmer to grow

details.summary: CGIAR is a global network of 15 international agricultural research centers that develop improved crop varieties, farming practices, and policies for food security. It was created in 1971 to build on the Green Revolution and remains the world's largest public agricultural research partnership.
details.whyItMatters: CGIAR research feeds hundreds of millions of people. Its centers developed IR8 rice, drought-tolerant maize, improved beans, and biofortified crops. Every dollar invested in CGIAR research returns an estimated $10 in economic benefit to developing.
takeaways: CGIAR consists of 15 research centers focused on food security and poverty reduction
Its centers have released thousands of improved crop varieties used worldwide
Every dollar invested in CGIAR returns an estimated $10 in benefits to developing nations

faq.question: What are the most important CGIAR research centers?
faq.answer: IRRI (Philippines) focuses on rice. CIMMYT (Mexico) focuses on wheat and maize. ICRISAT addresses crops for the semi-arid tropics. IITA works on African tropical crops. CIP specializes in potatoes and sweet potatoes.

faq.question: How is CGIAR research funded and governed?
faq.answer: CGIAR is funded by governments, foundations (Gates Foundation is a major donor), and development agencies totaling roughly $800 million annually. It is governed by a system council of funders and an independent advisory group. Research is conducted as public goods, freely available to all countries.
